title: OSHA Safety Glasses Checklist (29 CFR 1910.133)
subtitle: For on-site checks of eye and face protection wherever eye or face hazards are present.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A; use N/A only where the hazard or task is not present in the area checked.
When an item fails, stop the task until the correct protection is in place, and record the defect and the corrective action.
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks beyond this list.

sections.title: Protection in use
items: Every employee exposed to flying particles is wearing suitable eyewear or face protection during the task.
Workers exposed to molten metal have appropriate protection on and in position.
Workers exposed to liquid chemicals, acid or caustic liquids wear protection appropriate to that hazard.
Workers exposed to chemical vapors or gases wear protection suited to the hazard.
Workers exposed to light radiation that could injure the eyes wear appropriate protection.
Where flying objects are a hazard, the eyewear in use has side protection, built in or detachable.
Clip-on or slide-on side shields are fitted to the frame and are of a type that meets 1910.133.
Each employee wearing prescription lenses in operations with eye hazards wears protection with the prescription built in, or protection worn over the glasses.
Protection worn over prescription glasses leaves both the prescription lenses and the protective lenses in their proper position.

sections.title: Filter shades for arc welding and cutting
items: Workers exposed to injurious light radiation use equipment with filter lenses that have a shade number suited to the work.
Shade no lighter than 7, 8, 10 or 11 for arc current below 60, 60-160, 160-250 or 250-550 respectively.
Gas metal arc and flux cored arc welding
Shade no lighter than 7 below 60, and no lighter than 10 in the 60-160, 160-250 and 250-500 bands.
Shade no lighter than 8 up to 150 arc current, and no lighter than 10 at 150-500.
Shade no lighter than 10 for light work (below 500) and 11 for heavy work (500-1000).
Shade no lighter than 6, 8, 10 or 11 for arc current below 20, 20-100, 100-400 or 400-800 respectively.
With the arc in clear view, shade no lighter than 8 (below 300), 9 (300-400) or 10 (400-800).

sections.title: Filter shades for gas welding, oxygen cutting, brazing and soldering
items: Shade no lighter than 4 for plate under 1/8 in., 5 for 1/8 to 1/2 in., and 6 for plate over 1/2 in.
Shade no lighter than 3 for plate under 1 in., 4 for 1 to 6 in., and 5 for plate over 6 in.
The shade chosen gives a sufficient view of the weld zone and is not lighter than the table minimum for the operation.

sections.title: Marking and design standard
items: Each eye and face device carries a distinct marking that identifies its manufacturer.
Device markings or manufacturer documentation show compliance with ANSI/ISEA Z87.1-2010, ANSI Z87.1-2003 or ANSI Z87.1-1989 (R-1998).
Any device not made to one of those editions comes with the employer's demonstration that it protects at least as well as a conforming device.

references: 29 CFR 1910.133: Eye and face protection (Part 1910 Subpart I, Personal Protective Equipment)
